title: Translational dysregulation as a mechanistic driver of cognitive, behavioral, and affective phenotypes in FXS and TSC
title_zh: 翻译失调作为FXS和TSC认知、行为与情感表型的机制驱动因素
abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are characterized by a spectrum of cognitive, behavioral, and affective morbidities, reflecting underlying disruptions in neural circuit development. Emerging evidence implicates translational dysregulation of synaptic proteins as a central mechanistic driver of these disordered phenotypes. Translational dysregulation entails atypical mechanisms of impaired initiation, elongation, and mRNA targeting, causing imbalanced protein synthesis. In NDDs specifically, translation of synaptic proteins is perturbed across developing neurons. Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) and Fragile X Syndrome (FXS) are notable monogenic NDDs, in which mutations in regulatory genes (Tsc1/Tsc2 in TSC, Fmr1 in FXS) disrupt signaling pathways that converge on mTORC1, PERK, and ERK/MAPK proteins, and result in excessive or insufficient translation of key synaptic proteins. These translational imbalances eventually compromise synapse formation, dendritic spine maturation, and neuronal network connectivity, contributing to deficits in learning, memory, social behavior, and emotional regulation. This review highlights the molecular mechanisms by which aberrant protein synthesis contributes to the cognitive and behavioral manifestations of TSC and FXS. Importantly, we also highlight cell-type-specific mechanisms, illustrating how translational dysregulation differentially impacts distinct neuronal and glial populations to shape behavioral and cognitive outcomes. Understanding the links between translational control and neurodevelopmental outcomes provides critical insights into the pathophysiology of these disorders and informs the development of targeted therapeutic interventions aimed at restoring synaptic protein homeostasis.
abstract_zh: 神经发育障碍（NDDs）表现为认知、行为和情感方面的多样病理，反映了神经回路发育的潜在紊乱。新兴证据表明突触蛋白的翻译失调是这些异常表型的核心机制驱动因素。翻译失调涉及启动、延伸和mRNA靶向的异常机制，导致蛋白合成失衡。在NDDs中，突触蛋白的翻译在发育中的神经元中被扰乱。结节性硬化综合征（TSC）和脆性X综合征（FXS）是突出的单基因NDDs，其中调控基因（TSC中的Tsc1/Tsc2，FXS中的Fmr1）的突变破坏了与mTORC1、PERK和ERK/MAPK蛋白相交的信号通路，导致关键突触蛋白的过度或不足翻译。这些翻译失衡最终破坏突触形成、树突棘成熟和神经网络连通性，导致学习、记忆、社会行为和情绪调节的缺陷。本文综述了异常蛋白合成如何促成TSC和FXS的认知与行为表现的分子机制，并重点讨论了细胞类型特异性的机制，阐明翻译失调如何对不同的神经元和胶质细胞群体产生差异性影响，从而塑造行为和认知结果。了解翻译调控与神经发育结果之间的联系，为这些疾病的发病机制提供了关键见解，并为开发旨在恢复突触蛋白稳态的靶向治疗干预提供了依据。
